RELEVANT CHARACTER BACKGROUND

Aminata Diallo is a young construction worker in a bustling district on the outskirts of Bamako. She is the youngest person on her crew and the only woman on the site. She lives alone in a rented room with packed-earth walls and a corrugated tin roof, rises before dawn, and begins each day by carrying water from a communal stand because there is no tap in her room. She wears the same work trousers six days a week and spends long days hauling cement, stacking blocks, and checking measurements on the construction site.

She is trained by Sékou, an old master mason who lost two fingers to a faulty crane. He has trained her for two years, trusts her numbers, and treats her like a protégée rather than a favored equal. He teases her as “la petite comptable” because she recalculates load-bearing estimates in her head before lifting a trowel. She is also enrolled in an accounting course at a community center on the other side of the city, paying for it herself. She cannot afford the bus fare both ways, so she walks there, as she does for much of her travel. She keeps a small notebook tucked inside her shirt for figures and dates, and she studies at night by the light of a kerosene lamp until her eyes burn.

Aminata’s habits and values are shaped by hardship and loss. She internalized strict double-checking and self-reliance after her mother lost a market stall to a miscalculated loan. Her mother died when Aminata was twelve. She has counted everything since then: bricks, rice, weeks until exams, and other concrete quantities. She values counting and verification as the only trustworthy basis for decisions. She saves money methodically, keeps a fixed emergency fund hidden under a loose floorboard near her mattress, and never touches it or counts it in daylight. She keeps plans private because she believes spoken plans become exposed and vulnerable to being borrowed against. She does not speak openly about what she is saving for, even though she is saving not only for school and stability but also for a proper room with running water where her younger sister can live with her and attend school.

Her father once sold his tools to pay for a funeral and never held a trowel again, an event that stands in contrast to her own persistence in holding and using her tools every day. She is quiet and reserved, rarely speaking about her plans. She does not ask for advances on her wage. In work and daily life, she is precise, methodical, cautious, and attentive to detail. When faced with requests, she typically calculates the costs in time before answering. She routinely stays late to double-check measurements even without pay.

OBJECTIVE SITUATION

At the end of the workday, as the crew packs up, Sékou approaches Aminata at the site. He says the site manager needs someone to stay an extra hour that night to do the weekly inventory count before the next delivery arrives in the morning. The site manager is about to leave and tells Sékou to decide immediately. Sékou asks Aminata directly, “Decide now, little comptable. Do you take it?” There is no overtime pay, only responsibility. Aminata has her accounting notebook waiting at home and a long walk back. She must answer before Sékou turns away.

PRE-APPRAISAL STATE AND ACCESSIBLE MEMORIES

Aminata is physically exhausted after ten hours of hauling cement and stacking blocks. Her eyes burn from dust, and she faces a two-hour walk home if she leaves now. Her accounting notebook is at home, and the study session she had planned for tonight is already shortened. She is immediately aware of the time and effort implications of the request, along with the absence of overtime pay.

The phrase “weekly count” directly cues a recent inventory in which she was the only person who noticed that the cement bags on the delivery sheet did not match the pile. The site manager’s hurried tone also cues a prior experience of sudden financial pressure: her mother’s loan being called in without warning. These are directly accessible memories connected to the present request. Her established habits of calculation, careful verification, silence about plans, and reluctance to ask for advances are currently present as background conditions, not as a decided response.
